content: When a beehive is placed within range of a Paradox Flower's leaked mana, the bees inside instinctively alter their production.
They produce Propolis instead of honey, a sticky, resinous substance naturally used by bees to seal gaps and reinforce hive structure.
The mana saturation enhances propolis's natural adhesive properties, making it ideal for binding magical components together.
It's strong enough to hold materials under magical stress, yet malleable enough to allow controlled mana flow.
Critically, the bees themselves are not transformed. They remain ordinary bees, simply responding to their environment.
Note: This effect requires the beehive to remain near the flower. Moving the hive away from the flower's range will cause bees to revert to normal honey production.
Propolis is naturally adhesive and cohesive. When saturated with mana during production, it gains two critical properties:
Physical Bonding: Strong adhesive that holds magical components together under stress. Essential for wand construction. It prevents the core from separating from the handle.
Mana Insulation/Conduction: When applied as a thick seal, propolis prevents magical energy from leaking.
When used as a thin binding layer, it allows controlled mana flow while maintaining structural integrity.
This dual nature makes propolis irreplaceable in early magical crafting.
